conventions.convention: Work over C with integer r ≥ 1, orthogonal idempotent basis e_i, coordinatewise multiplication, unit Σ_i e_i, and nonzero complex weights w_i. The counit and coproduct satisfy ε(e_i)=w_i and Δ(e_i)=w_i⁻¹ e_i⊗e_i.
The closed oriented cobordism category permits parametrized circle boundaries and no free boundary. The construction asserts neither an open sector nor a fully extended point-level theory.
H=μ∘Δ, genus g is a nonnegative integer, and the connected closed amplitude is ε(H^g(η(1))), including g=0.
The involution fixes each e_i and conjugates coefficients. The form h(a,b)=ε(a*b) is conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second; positivity concerns this specified form.
For the dual-number example, x²=0, ε(1)=0, ε(x)=1, and the conjugate-linear involution fixes x. Semisimplicity means vanishing Jacobson radical, defined as the intersection of maximal left ideals.

load_bearing.statement: For A=⊕_{i=1}^r C e_i with e_i e_j=δ_ij e_i and w_i∈C×, ε(e_i)=w_i and Δ(e_i)=w_i⁻¹e_i⊗e_i define a finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebra. The closed classification supplies its TQFT with Z_A(Σ_g)=ε(H^g(η(1))), H=μ∘Δ.
The connected closed genus-g amplitude is Z_A(Σ_g)=Σ_{i=1}^r w_i^{1-g}. The cylinder acts by 1_A, and the torus amplitude is r.
The form h is a Hermitian positive-definite inner product exactly when every weight w_i is a positive real number. The algebraic closed oriented TQFT exists for every nonzero complex weight.

concerns.concern: The Definition first sets “1_A=Σ_i e_i” as an algebra element, then says “the cylinder acts by 1_A.” The latter denotes an endomorphism and should be distinguished as id_A. The same overload propagates into prop-qftx-frobenius-genus-amplitude, whose F2 also writes H^0=1_A. The intended identity action is clear from the classification supplier; the notation conflates an element with a map.
